A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer satisfiability research despite the changed title and terminology. The text, equations, figures, and scientific Appendices A–C support a complete comparison. V2 removes v1's administrative checklist, not its proof appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical definitions, complexity results, and proofs, with no original empirical outcomes. Its checklist also marks experimental questions as not applicable.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The added diagrams and application examples are explanatory, not experimental results.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, attention mechanisms, arithmetic restrictions, and tiling-reduction constructions are retained. Renaming encoder-only transformers (EOT) to transformer encoders (TE) and adding an architecture diagram do not change the model.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. V2's key-value verification and spam-detection examples are hypothetical illustrations, not added evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods or baselines. References to verification systems and transformer expressiveness remain related-work discussion.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical evaluation protocols. Input-length bounds and precision restrictions remain unchanged theoretical conditions, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary experimental analyses. V2's new illustrations explain existing constructions rather than adding analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests. Removing checklist questions marked not applicable does not remove statistical evidence.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. The reported undecidability, NP/NEXPTIME complexity, and fixed-width-arithmetic conclusions also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit definition of relative expressiveness through realization of the same functions. Section 1 revises the soundness/completeness characterization, removing v1's explicit false-otherwise clause. The theorem statements, lemmas, and proofs in Appendices A–C otherwise remain unchanged apart from notation and formatting.

C1.justification: The new title and abstract foreground satisfiability more directly, but retain the same contributions: undecidability, bounded-input complexity, and upper and lower bounds under fixed-width arithmetic. The scientific scope and strength of these claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of finite precision and implications for formal reasoning are retained. Section 6 preserves the hardmax versus softmax uncertainty, embedding–attention tradeoff, and arithmetic-specific open questions; adding 'limitations' to its heading does not introduce new limitations.

D1.justification: The detailed mathematical constructions and parameter choices in the appendices are retained. Neither version supplies experimental implementation details or a code/data release; the omitted checklist contained no such reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and main related-work discussion are retained. Section 2 newly identifies Hao et al. (2022) as the closest syntactic formulation and contextualizes differing transformer definitions using Strobl et al. (2024), providing a limited positioning refinement.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and EOT terminology, rewrites the abstract and selected explanatory and concluding paragraphs, reorganizes Section 3, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. The main section sequence and scientific appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Visual exposition expands substantially with a transformer architecture diagram (Figure 1) and a tiling-reduction illustration (Figure 3). V1's complexity diagram is retained as Figure 2. The document also adopts ICLR formatting, with redesigned title/author presentation, headings, page headers, and reference layout.

improvement.justification: The added architecture and tiling diagrams, concrete motivating examples, and explicit expressiveness definition make the framework easier to follow while preserving all scientific proofs. This is a modest expository gain, tempered by the soundness/completeness rewrite dropping v1's explicit false-case condition. The principal results and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
